Target periodogram from a list of orbital periods (period2spectrum.m)

Source: R/coco_target_from_periods.R
coco_target_from_periods.Rd

Sum of sinusoids at the orbital periods, sampled from t1 to t2 (kyr), and its zero-padded periodogram between f1 and f2 (cycles/kyr).

Usage

coco_target_from_periods(
  orbit = NULL,
  age_ma = NULL,
  t1 = 3e+05,
  t2 = 308000,
  step = 1,
  f1 = 0,
  f2 = NULL,
  pad = 10000,
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

orbit

Astronomical periods of the target sinusoids, in kyr (numeric vector, > 0; sorted longest first internally), e.g. c(405, 125, 95, 41, 23, 22, 19). NULL uses the nine periods at age_ma. Default=NULL.

age_ma

Age in Ma (single numeric value, 0 to 4429) at which the nine periods are taken from orbit9_at_age (La2004 g and s frequencies with the AstroGeo22 precession constant); only used when orbit is NULL, and one of the two must be given. Default=NULL.

t1, t2

Start and end of the time axis on which the synthetic sum of sinusoids is sampled, in kyr (numeric, t2 > t1); the length t2 - t1 sets the width of the target peaks. Default=300000 and Default=308000.

step

Time step of the synthetic series, in kyr (numeric, > 0). Default=1.

f1

Lowest frequency of the target that is returned, in cycles/kyr (numeric, >= 0). Default=0.

f2

Highest frequency of the target that is returned, in cycles/kyr (numeric, > f1); NULL uses 1.2 times the highest orbital frequency, as in the Acycle GUI. Default=NULL.

pad

Length (number of points) to which the synthetic series is zero-padded for the periodogram (integer; at least the series length is used); a larger value gives a finer frequency grid. Default=10000.

weights

Amplitudes of the sinusoids, one per period in orbit after sorting longest first (numeric vector). NULL uses 1.0 for eccentricity, 0.8 for obliquity and 0.6 for precession (for nine periods via coco_fixed_target_weights; otherwise the three longest get 1.0, the fourth 0.8 and the rest 0.6, as in Acycle period2spectrum.m). Default=NULL.

Value

two-column matrix: frequency (cycles/kyr), power

Details

The returned target carries attribute "orbit" so coco_classic() uses the same periods to count contributing parameters.
